_README: Curated laws for ds_contract, merged onto the primitive it names. Absence of an entry means nobody has written the law yet — NOT that anything is permitted. Keep this small: a rule here is a rule an agent will follow, and a stale one is worse than none. Every entry cites where the decision was taken. A key here is a COMPONENT ID — overrides merge onto the inventory walk by id, so an entry named after a token constant (KIOSK_UTILITY_SHEET) merges onto nothing and is law no agent can find. A token's law lives in its docblock, which ds_tokens serves as the `use` sentence on that axis.

DeskStageContext.useWhen: fullscreen, expand the table, stage state, is this table on a desk, desk stage, maximize the grid
DeskStageContext.doNot: Do not add a second fullscreen state. The one state has two faces: DataTableFullscreenToggle on a table row and DeskRecordViewSwitch (In place / Split) in the record header band that DeskRecordPlane paints in both views (operator 2026-09-26: the staffer chooses and can see which view they are in). DeskPageChrome OWNS the state and publishes it here; the control lives on the table's own toolbar row (DataTableFullscreenToggle), which renders NOTHING when useDeskStageOptional() is null — a station embed or a modal-hosted table has no stage to expand, and a dead control is worse than no control. Do not move the toggle up to the page header: in fullscreen that header is not rendered.
DeskStageContext.law: src/design-system/components/DeskStageContext.tsx. Operator 2026-08-30: the fullscreen control belongs on the table's row, not the page's.

DeskStageOverlay.useWhen: multi-field form on a desk, edit form over the table, inset form, row action form (release, revoke, unlink), config editor opened from a pencil, where does a form go, right rail or overlay
DeskStageOverlay.doNot: Do NOT mount this with fill="stage" to show a picked row's record: a record is placed by DeskRecordPlane, which drives this overlay for the in-place view and draws the fullscreen split itself. Do NOT put a multi-field form in the legacy right rail (DetailStackRailRegistrar / useRegisterRightPanel detail priority / a hand-rolled evidence aside). Use this directly for fill="inset" forms over the still-mounted table (Center Lock Q5): a row verb's form, or the editor behind a record's one-line config summary + pencil (org config that outlives the record — rules, roles — lives on a config page, never as record data). One value on a cell is a Popover, not this; irreversible is a confirm Dialog. The legacy right rail stays for `supporting` tools over the whole table, scan-station edges and linked peeks only.
DeskStageOverlay.law: src/design-system/components/DeskStageOverlay.tsx; src/components/tables/table-surface-binding.ts TableRecordPlane (Center Lock Q5). Operator 2026-09-25: records open through DeskRecordPlane (in place by default, split in fullscreen); this overlay keeps the inset form role.

DeskRecordPlane.useWhen: open a row, record view, order details, record detail, selected order, selected carton, task detail, daily item detail, where does the detail go, inspector, side panel for a row, fullscreen with list and details, split view, list on the left and details on the right, master detail, evidence column, J/K walk records
DeskRecordPlane.doNot: Do NOT hand-roll a split or an evidence aside; do NOT register a record with RightRailHost (DetailStackRailRegistrar / useRegisterRightPanel detail priority); do NOT mount DeskStageOverlay fill="stage" for a record outside this primitive. One record component, two views, the STAFFER chooses (operator 2026-09-25): fullscreen off → in place of the fixed-width list (DeskStageOverlay fill="stage", list still mounted); fullscreen on (DataTableFullscreenToggle, remembered per staffer per desk as `desk.<deskId>.fullscreen`) → list left, record right at DESK_SPLIT_RECORD_CLASS. Pass the list as `list` (mounted once; never remount it between views), the record as children, the walk as indexLabel/onPrev/onNext; the surface owns J/K (useRecordCursorKeyboard with `escape: false`, or its own handler), the plane owns Esc (first Esc closes the record, next exits fullscreen). Mark list rows with DESK_RECORD_KEY_ATTR + `recordKey` so Esc returns focus to the exact row. Lay the record out with DeskRecordLayout (main 2/3 + aside 1/3 on the stage, stacked in the pane — a container query, never md:/lg:); simple records omit `aside`. Show only the sections the current mode needs; keep the surface's deep-link param (?openOrderId=, ?task=, ?check=, ?openRepair=).

Operator 2026-09-25: fixed-width list with the record in its place by default; fullscreen is the staffer's choice of a list-left / record-right split.

DeskActionSlot.useWhen: page CTA, primary action on a desk, overall action, leading action, Labels left of Sync, Labels display toggle, Export in the Sync dropdown, register an action into the page header, Add button on a workbench, desk action slot
DeskActionSlot.doNot: Do not pass a CTA down as a prop through the route-group layout — a shared frame that imports one desk's intake stops being shared. The active surface registers with DeskActionSlotRegistrar (role=primary for the create verb, role=overall for collection actions such as Media Export, role=leading for To-ship Labels immediately left of primary). Last writer wins per role, so Labels does not replace Add. A desk with no CTA registers nothing and the slot stays empty. Memoize the node — a fresh element identity every render re-registers every render, which loops through the provider. The node is DeskHeaderAction (Button with radius pill locked) or DeskHeaderSplitAction for a split intake (it reads the bar's face; never pass embeddedChrome yourself) — never a raw Button with a rounded-* class, never radius flush in this slot. Print, filter, columns, zoom and fullscreen stay off this row. To-ship Export is not an overall header button — DeskExportMenuRegistrar tucks it into the Sync Google Sheet dropdown (operator 2026-09-01). Labels is a display toggle for the paperwork walk (pressed = walk on), not a per-row print verb.

Operator 2026-09-01: overall actions (Export) sit in the header cluster left of the primary CTA on desks that still own a collection Export; To-ship tucks Export into the Sync dropdown. Operator 2026-09-01: To-ship Labels is role=leading, immediately left of Sync, and toggles the paperwork display. Owner 2026-09-24: on the industrial bar (DeskPageChrome stage=flush) the bar provides the segment face — header actions render as flush mono cells with no gap or padding between them, full bar height, pressed = ink fill, exactly like the mode tabs on the bar's left end. The desk never picks the face.

TableStatusBar.useWhen: row count, shown of total, selected count, copy selection, table foot strip, sub-mode tabs inside one page tab, selection CTA hotkey reveal, idle-left path readout lead
TableStatusBar.doNot: Do not wire NEW page modes into its `tabs` props. Page modes ride DeskPageChrome's TOP row on every desk AND every scan station (operator 2026-08-31) — the desk-threaded `tabStrip` plumbing was deleted the same day. What this strip is for is the right half (shown / total / selected / copy), which is the one thing a table knows and a frame does not; its tab half survives only for SECOND-level sub-modes inside a single page tab. Idle-left `lead` is a context readout (date/folder path) — never a CTA, never page navigation, never painted beside selection pills (precedence: selectionActions beat tabs beat lead). `lead` is not DeskPageChrome's `tabsLead`. Do not hand-roll a teaching `<kbd>` for selection hotkeys — mount KeyboardKey. Do not leave standing letters, open a cheat sheet from staff `?` while CTAs are mounted, add a foot `?`, park keycaps outside, or widen via iconRight/gap.

DeskPageChrome.useWhen: page header, page title, page-level primary action, in-page tabs, workbench frame, desk frame, non-scan desk, fixed-width stage, detached table card, table fullscreen
DeskPageChrome.doNot: Do not hand-roll a page title row, a tab strip, or a `max-w-*` stage on any non-scan desk. Scope: operator DESKS only — settings/admin pages and detail panels keep PageHeader from @/components/ui/pane-header, and a full-canvas surface (/studio) takes neither — this is the frame, and a second one is a fork. Scan stations mount it too (operator 2026-08-31) — /unbox, /pack, /test, /triage, /shipping/scan-out wear the same frame, and their mode tabs ride the TOP row, never a TableStatusBar foot strip. A station passes its tabs explicitly because they are body-switchers, not nav children. Do not pass a title literal — the title is nav data, threaded by @/components/desk/DeskPageLayout off the page's SIDEBAR_PAGE_NAV label, so the header cannot drift from the spine. Do not also paint the page name as a GlobalHeader HeaderPageSwitcher chip on desks — that switcher is Scan Stations triage only (operator 2026-08-31). Do not pull the tablist with `-ml-3` to align the first label — the active tab's border-b is on the hit box and hangs off the row hairline. Every tab keeps `px-3` so the name sits inside the underline; do not `first:pl-0`. Do not put the CTA back on the tab row, do not use role-display for the title (role-title, 18px/600), do not animate the tab underline between tabs, and do not add a second measure token: DESK_STAGE_MAX_PX is the one desk width. `tabsLead` is the tab row's ONLY slot and it is not a second CTA — it takes a control on the SAME axis as the tabs (Media Library's media-type overflow, which writes the same param through the same function). An action goes in the header CTA; a row refinement goes on the table's toolbar. In fullscreen the header and tab row are NOT rendered — never re-parent the search or the fullscreen toggle, they already live on the table's own row in both states.

CopyChip.useWhen: copy chip, last-8, order number, tracking, serial, purchase order, sku, identifier, clipboard, OrderIdChip, TrackingChip, SerialChip, PoChip
CopyChip.doNot: Do not hand-roll a copyable id span. Use the named variant (OrderIdChip, TrackingChip, SerialChip, PoChip, …) when one exists. Tones live in CHIP_TONES — do not invent a hue. Hover menu is CopyChipHoverMenu, not a fork. Not a status chip (that is badge or StatusBadge). TRUNCATION (operator 2026-09-12): abbreviate on a DELIMITER, never at a blind offset. `getLast8` is `raw.slice(-8)`, so `113-1397006-0292212` renders `-0292212` — a leading dash that reads as a negative number or a system error to someone scanning a column at speed, and that makes the column edge jagged because a separator carries different visual weight than a digit. Prefer the last delimiter-bounded segment (`0292212`); fall back to the last 8 characters ONLY when the id has no delimiter; then strip any leading non-alphanumerics from the result. NEVER pad an identifier to a fixed width. `5034` is not `00005034`: staff read these aloud and key them into an RF scanner, and a padded id is a WRONG id. Uniformity comes from right-alignment plus `font-mono tabular-nums` — the right edge is the scanning line — not from falsifying the value. A leading `#` on an order chip is the HashIcon glyph (identifier-class marker), not a truncation artifact: do not strip it.
CopyChip.law: src/components/ui/CopyChip.tsx — CHIP_TONES is the hue SoT; HashIcon is the identifier glyph. src/lib/copy-chip-format.ts — getLast8 / getLast8Serial are the abbreviation SoT. Operator 2026-08-31: pin the house copy-chip family. Operator 2026-09-12: blind last-8 orphans separators; cut on a delimiter, strip leading symbols, never zero-pad, monospace + right-align for the uniform column.

CompoundSelectStatusFace.useWhen: row status icon, urgent lightning bolt, flashing status glyph, out of stock alert in a row, triage mark, select gutter at rest, status on non-hover, contextual select column, multi-status row icon
CompoundSelectStatusFace.doNot: Do not add a status COLUMN or a second glyph beside the checkbox — the resting face and the selection square share one 16px box, and the pointer chooses (hover / keyboard focus / `(hover: none)` hand it back to GridSelectSquareFace). Do not resolve which mark to paint yourself: compoundSelectStatusMarks is the resolver (heat order — urgent rail, then attention rail or itemStatus, never the same kind twice). Do not paint a glyph on an ordinary row — the 2026-09-04 ruling against a resting mark on every row still stands. Do not give a row with two marks two glyphs side by side, or drop one as "less bad": the box ALTERNATES (one layer per mark, edgeMarkFlashOpacity index/count). Do not hand-roll the flash with animate / animate-pulse — every marked row shares one rAF clock so they pulse together; reduced motion stands the hottest mark still. Do not attach a tooltip or aria label: reaching for it replaces it, and the rail plus the item track already name the fact.

SlotTableGroupParentRow.useWhen: fold parent band, multi-line order band, group header row, parent row of a fold, collapse chevron row, group selection feedback, band status rollup
SlotTableGroupParentRow.doNot: Do not hand-roll a group header row — every fold parent on every PRODUCT_TABLES peer mounts this one (To-ship QueueGroupRow, Unbox ReceivingGridGroupRow). Its select gutter is the SAME contextual face as a leaf: `chrome="hover"` + `statuses` from compoundSelectStatusMarks over the group rollup, pinned top (COMPOUND_GUTTER_MARK_TOP_PIN_CLASS) and inset past the rail, with the fold chevron in COMPOUND_GUTTER_CHEVRON_BAND_CLASS under it. The fold chevron is hover-ONLY in every state — collapsed and expanded (operator 2026-09-15) — while the button keeps its hit plane and aria-expanded label; never leave a standing chevron and never gate the control instead of the glyph. SELECTION FEEDBACK: the band washes through `ledgerRowFillClass({ selected: checked === true })`, the same cascade the leaves use — never a bespoke blue, never a wash on `'mixed'` (that claims a membership the group has not got), never `bg-surface-canvas` (a gray band reads as disabled) and never transparent (frozen cells are `bg-inherit`). The band's status pill rolls up the resolver its leaves paint (`resolveRowStatus(row, queueMode)`), not a raw status column.

The MARK (checklist square + resting status glyph) is pinned to the TOP through COMPOUND_GUTTER_MARK_TOP_PIN_CLASS — the 2026-09-04 `items-start pt-1` ruling STANDS and a 2026-09-15 pass that floated it to the row's middle was reverted by the operator ("the checklist icon should be pinned to the top and the drop-down icon should be below the checklist icon"). Never put the child rail in the select gutter — its first 3px are CompoundEdgeRail, which is per-row and conditional, so one 3px slot would mean "urgent" on one row and "child" on the next. Never restore bg-text-default on either mark (operator 2026-09-15 retired the black rule), never a 4-side envelope or inner box, never a second bar. Do not swap the inset for a spacing token — it is the rail's own measurement, used twice.
compound-row-chrome.law: src/components/tables/compound/compound-row-chrome.ts. SLOT_TABLE_PAINT_LAW.selectGutterStatus + leafDetailSelect. ProgressBar.useWhen: progress meter, completion bar, stage progress, percent done, N of M, goal against actual, segmented increments, Duolingo-style step bar, mobile-first step progress
ProgressBar.doNot: Do not animate width, height, or position — the fill is a scaleX transform with transformOrigin:'left' and w-full, gated by useReducedMotion. Law M1 bans layout tweens; transform was struck from that ban 2026-08-25, so the fill is legal only in that form. Duration is framerDuration.progressFill (100ms), never an inline literal. Progression is a COUNT, never a pointer position: pass satisfied-required-steps over total-required, so a pointer sitting on step 5 of 8 does not render 5/8. The `segments` prop is the touch/mobile-first face (operator 2026-09-14): N discrete increments, per-segment scaleX fill of the SAME law, aria progressbar wiring on the wrapper. Do not hand-roll a second segmented bar anywhere — kiosk, /m, or desk.
ProgressBar.law: docs/warehouse-os/PROGRESSION-INTERVIEW-LEDGER.md — PG12 (segmented squares + a scaleX fill; M1 stands unamended), PG6 (percent-done is a count, never a position), PD1 (this file's width tween was the violation). Operator 2026-09-14: PG12's segmented face is now real via `segments`.

StepProgressHeader.useWhen: step-flow header band, mobile-first wizard header, X close left + progress segments middle + n/N count right, kiosk pane form header, /m step flow header, Duolingo-style progress header
StepProgressHeader.doNot: Do not compose a step-flow header from a title band plus an inline meter — this band IS the header (operator 2026-09-14: 'all in one header, X top left, progress bar, one-out-of-ten top right'). Do not hand-roll the bar: it composes ProgressBar with `segments={total}`. The count counts COMPLETED units (PG6), never the index of the step in view. Do not add a pane title inside this band — the step eyebrow in the body names the current step. Back affordances inside a fixed-width form measure use this X when 'exit the flow' is the semantic; paged back-steps belong to the body, not this band.
StepProgressHeader.law: Operator 2026-09-14 — 'think Duolingo instead of text'; kiosk DS unification Phase 1. Composes ProgressBar (PG12/PG6/M1). Mounts: KioskRepairPane and KioskCartLedger, both via KioskPaneForm `progress`. Every mount's segment count is a gate table (repairStepGates, cartStepGates), never a step index.

ProcedureDeck.useWhen: station work surface, procedure steps, step column, work list, guided procedure, unbox steps, the surface an operator works a station from
ProcedureDeck.doNot: Do not gate capture on the active step. Evidence claims the step it belongs to, so the pointer is a HINT about what to capture next, never an authority that rejects input — scanning what step 5 wants while the pointer sits on step 2 satisfies step 5, and steps 3-4 stay open and unticked. Do not auto-complete the steps in between. Every step stays mounted from the first frame (existing invariant 1) — that is what makes a jumped-past open step visible without a scroll, so do not virtualize or collapse the list.
ProcedureDeck.law: docs/warehouse-os/PROGRESSION-INTERVIEW-LEDGER.md — PG6 (evidence claims its own step; progression is non-linear), PG3 (evidence advances the pointer).

StepStateBadge.useWhen: step state mark, procedure step box, done/skipped/pending mark, checklist square
StepStateBadge.doNot: Do not make it clickable and do not render a rounded-full dot. A step is evidence-derived — a square that clicks to tick reintroduces the banned hand-ticked checklist. `skipped` keeps the chevron and never the check: a skip is a recorded waiver that a person looked and moved past, not a claim the work happened, and a required step skipped this way carries a deviation reason. One mark serves both ProcedureChecklist and ProcedureDeck; do not fork it per view.
StepStateBadge.law: File docblock (shape + evidence-derived). docs/warehouse-os/PROGRESSION-INTERVIEW-LEDGER.md — PG3 (evidence advances; tick is the fallback), PG8 (a skipped required step is a recorded deviation), PG1 (one derivation at two altitudes).

calendar.useWhen: calendar, date picker, day picker, month grid, shadcn calendar, 21st.dev calendar, react-day-picker
calendar.doNot: Do not import 'react-day-picker/style.css'. Do not drop relative or w-fit from the root, and do not simplify nav to inset-x-0 top-0: the p-3 root makes those offsets wrong by 12px vertically and 16px horizontally. Range picking is calendar-range-select, not this with mode="range" hand-styled. A full field (trigger + popover + Apply) is DateRangePickerField or DateRangePickerPill, not this bare. Do not mount this as an inline table date editor. Slot-table ship-by / due date / pick a date in a cell is DateRangePickerField variant="compact" (not variant=range).

ItemCardRow.doNot: Do not round or elevate repeated rows. The phone is one white sheet; rows separate with ITEM_RECORD_MOBILE_ROW.shell hairlines. Orders, Picks and Shipping all mount this same component. Query ds_tokens({ axis: 'item-record', query: 'row' }).

SearchResultRow.useWhen: search result row, find result, hit row, ranked result list, ⌘K result, /search results, browse hit, SearchResultRow
SearchResultRow.doNot: Do not fork this row — it is the ONE result row for the header preview, ⌘K, /search and every rail. Do not add a 3-dot (⋮) menu: click-to-select is the whole interaction and search rows carry zero row menus by design. Gate chrome on the `density` prop (compact | comfortable | dropdown), NEVER on a `md:`/`lg:` breakpoint — a desktop sidebar rail is narrow too, and a viewport query corrupts it. LAYOUT (operator 2026-09-12): the VERIFIABLE IDENTIFIER owns the leading column, because a warehouse reader scans top-to-bottom down the left edge. Do not seat a text-heavy status word (“UNASSIGNED”, “OPEN”) in that premier slot. Status is a minimal dot + concise badge sitting WITH the id, never a coloured dot on one edge of the row and its word on the other — that splits one fact across the full width and forces two fixations to read a single state. Do not repeat the entity noun (“Order”) under every title: it is the same on every row, so it is noise that costs a line which a real fact (qty, bin, exact stamp) should own. A relative stamp (“4d”) is not sufficient alone for SLA work — carry the exact timestamp with it. If a surface needs uniform columns, click-to-sort headers and operational fields, it wants the ONE TABLE ENGINE (DataTable), not a restyled list: a read plane is a MOUNT.

Operator 2026-09-12: id leads the row in monospace, status is a dot + badge beside it, the redundant entity label goes, and a loose list that wants columns becomes a DataTable mount. MobileShell.law: src/components/mobile/redesign/MobileShell.tsx · docs/mobile-first/SURFACE_LAW.md §4/§7 · src/lib/mobile/mobile-first-surface.ts. Operator 2026-09-10: every operator verb must be completable on /m first.

BottomSheet.useWhen: edit sheet from the /info pencil, hub dock verb form, confirmation sheet, picker sheet (choose a value, staff, reason, type), quick look at a linked item from inside another record (an item linked to a ticket), mobile sheet
BottomSheet.doNot: Never the PRIMARY record of the job being worked — an order while picking or packing, a carton, a unit, a bin, a SKU, a ticket. That is a full scrollable screen: the entity's hub on DetailHubScreen (/m/<entity>/[id]), opened as a route, with an X back to the job (MobileDetailTopBar close). A sheet is only for a quick look at a LINKED item from inside another record, an edit, a dock verb, a confirm or a picker. Lists on phone are flat hairline work rows — never rounded/elevated islands and never a DataTable as the phone SoT (SURFACE_LAW §5). Do not open a desk dialog or a RightRailHost detail.

DetailHubScreen.useWhen: mobile scanned entity hub, mobile record detail, phone drill-in, entity details and edit, phone record screen, scanned thing detail, repair hub, SKU exception hub, unit hub, bin hub, handling unit hub, receiving carton hub, order hub, scan-out hub, mobile exoskeleton, DetailRecordFrame, /info screen frame, job screen frame
DetailHubScreen.doNot: The hub is EDGE TO EDGE (operator 2026-09-25): no page padding and no gaps; card, ack, content and door rows run the full width, separated by one border-mode-rule; only text keeps its inset, and a content slot owns its own inset. Never wrap the slots in px-mode-page or space-y, and never box the card or the door list — full-bleed rows are what later left/right swipe actions attach to. This is the ONE record grammar on /m (the repair hub exoskeleton). Do not hand-roll a hub from ModeRegion + MobileDetailTopBar + cards: mount DetailHubScreen with card = a DetailSummaryCard mapper (whole card → /info), rows = detailDoor(base, id, title, icon, { meta, enabled }) doors from @/lib/mobile/detail-door, dock = DetailDock (≤3 verbs, one primary) — or MobileCaptureWindow when the hub's job is scanning, and put the dock's sheets in children. /info and each job screen mount DetailRecordFrame. Never put a heading above the card, an Edit button or pencil on the hub (the only edit is the /info bar pencil opening a BottomSheet), router.back()/router.push for Back (backHref), a nested <main>, useEffect+fetch for hub facets (React Query, qk.<entity>.hub), a hand-rolled sticky bottom bar, or MobileTriagePage / ItemCardRow / a row → BottomSheet as an entity record. A new hub route goes into DETAIL_HUB_PEERS; porting one drops DETAIL_HUB_UNPORTED_BASELINE.
DetailHubScreen.law: src/design-system/components/DetailHubScreen.tsx · docs/handoff/mobile-ds-law-exoskeleton-HANDOFF.md. Operator 2026-09-24: one grammar for every scanned thing — a compact information display on top, then grouped into exact actions (photos, …) below; delete the old mobile display rules rather than keep them beside it.

DetailSummaryCard.useWhen: hub summary card, card slot of DetailHubScreen, compact entity card, read-only record preview, scan detail summary, repair hub card, unit hub card, SKU exception card
DetailSummaryCard.doNot: Full-bleed, no border box and no radius (operator 2026-09-25: edge to edge); the hub draws the rule under it. This is the first, read-only preview of ONE scanned entity — never a dashboard tile, a list-row replacement, or a second editable form. Exactly one full-width title (truncate), at most two job-relevant caption lines, a mono identifier bottom-left and one status chip bottom-right. The ID and chip MUST share box height (transparent border + py-0.5 on the ID; border + py-0.5 on the chip). The WHOLE card opens the entity's /info screen; do not put a pencil, Edit text, status selector, or another button on the card. The ONLY edit pencil is in the /info top bar. Do not put a heading such as Information above the card. It fills the card slot of DetailHubScreen (map an entity onto it, e.g. RepairInfoCard); the hub, not the card, mounts DetailNav doors and the <=3-verb DetailDock. Pick and pack hubs open their existing task runner rather than embedding its steps.
DetailSummaryCard.law: src/design-system/components/DetailSummaryCard.tsx · docs/handoff/mobile-entity-exoskeleton-HANDOFF.md. Operator 2026-09-24: simple first view; details on tap; status bottom-right; customer phone in the preview; pencil only in the expanded view.

DetailDock.useWhen: mobile entity hub verbs, hub dock, thumb-zone verbs, bottom action dock, edge-to-edge bottom bar, flush verb bar, repair hub actions, SKU exception actions, scanned entity verbs, mobile exoskeleton dock, scan dock, serial scan bottom, scan button, job CTA bar, next unit bar, selection bar, batch action bar, single full-width bottom button, inline verb band, row verbs, take and pass buttons, board row actions, order card actions, 2x2 action grid under a record, scan in the middle of the bottom bar, centred scan button
DetailDock.doNot: At most three verbs and exactly one primary. The bar is FLUSH (operator 2026-09-25: "no padded top, left and right for the buttons, must be edge to edge"): verbs fill the bar edge to edge with square corners and no gap, a 1px border-mode-rule between adjacent verbs, only the safe-area inset below — never wrap it in page padding, re-add a grid gap, or pass rounded-mode to its cells. It is the ONLY surface on a hub that changes the entity: never add verbs to the summary card, the top bar, or the door rows. Do not hand-roll a sticky bottom nav with a Button grid on a hub; that is this component. It is also every phone screen's bottom execution bar (operator 2026-09-25, industrial terminal block): 72px flush cells (min-h-18), instant ink inversion on press (no transition, no scale), a leading-edge 500ms lock so a double-tap fires once, and a press buzz where the Vibration API exists. State 3 — a one-job screen (Next unit, Scan another label) passes ONE verb and it fills the bar; State 2 — a selection passes selection={{ count, onClear }} and a dark 30% dismiss cell (✕ N SEL) leads ≤2 verbs. Never hand-roll a sticky bottom bar for a job CTA or a selection bar; never bring global navigation to the bottom (it lives in MobileSidebarDrawer). Scanning is NOT a dock verb: a screen whose job is scanning (serials into a visit, labels into a queue) mounts MobileCaptureWindow (src/components/mobile/station/MobileCaptureWindow.tsx) as its bottom surface — lens, collapsed Scan bar to re-arm, and its keyed fallback for typing a code by hand — or it has no scan at all. Never a Scan verb that opens the window, never a hand-rolled typed-entry bar beside it (operator 2026-09-25). A verb that NAVIGATES to /m/scan ("Scan again") is not a scanner and stays a verb. INLINE (owner 2026-09-26, pick edge-to-edge): placement="inline" is the same band in-flow under a record (a list row, an order card) — full width with a border-t rule, not sticky, no safe-area pad, up to four verbs (four = flush 2×2, 1px rules both ways), 48px cells whose labels wrap and never truncate. Never hand-roll a padded grid-cols-2 gap-2 of bordered Buttons under a row; that is this. CENTRED SCAN (owner 2026-09-26): on a scanning job screen the camera's collapsed Scan bar is the dock's MIDDLE cell between two verbs, in its success fill for hierarchy — pass it via MobileCaptureWindow collapsedFrame={(scan) => <DetailDock center={scan} …/>}; never a Scan row stacked above the dock, and never a Scan verb of your own. With the lens up, the dock renders alone under the panel.
DetailDock.law: src/design-system/components/DetailDock.tsx · docs/handoff/mobile-entity-exoskeleton-HANDOFF.md (DetailDock, from RepairWorkbenchDock) · docs/handoff/fnsku-reprint-HANDOFF.md (flush bar). Operator 2026-09-24: repair hub is the reference for every scanned entity. · docs/design-system/HANDOFF-pick-edge-to-edge.md (inline placement).

KioskChip.useWhen: kiosk chip, counter tablet pill, touch chip, selectable reason pill, fact chip on a kiosk card, kiosk cart line facts, rounded pill for a tablet

KioskCartLineCard.useWhen: kiosk cart line, cart line row, counter tablet cart list item, kiosk cart card, customer-facing cart line
KioskCartLineCard.doNot: A cart line is a CARD, never a CompoundRow / DataTable — SURFACE_LAW §5: lists on a phone-shaped surface are cards. The card is FLAT: it sits on the flat KIOSK_UTILITY_SHEET, so separation is `border-border-hairline` + MOBILE_SCAN_ROW_CORNER, never elevationClass — a shadow inside a sheet the operator already de-shadowed is the same popover cue one altitude down (2026-09-15). The card IS the edit affordance (tap to correct); void stays the swipe verb on KioskCartSwipeRow. Staff and customer faces mount the SAME card — `readOnly` drops the interaction, not the anatomy. KioskCartLineCard.law: src/components/kiosk/KioskCartLineCard.tsx · src/lib/kiosk/cart-card-view.ts · docs/mobile-first/SURFACE_LAW.md §5. Kiosk DS unification Phase 2, 2026-09-14; flattened 2026-09-15 with the sheet.

KioskTicketStep.useWhen: kiosk support ticket choice, link existing ticket on a tablet, create new ticket at the counter, attach a repair drop-off to a helpdesk ticket, kiosk ticket picker, counter ticket candidate list, create-or-link slider under a signature
KioskTicketStep.doNot: NOT its own step, not mounted flat, and not a stacked pill pair. It rides UNDER the signature pad inside Review & sign, revealed by the ink: operator 2026-09-15 asked for it 'after the customer has submitted their signature', then collapsed the fifth step ('because the stepper is full at that review and sign step, would it be best to include a slider … below the signature so it would be mounted under one step?'), then simplified the control ('the create new and the link existing should be simplified into just one slider where you would be able to slide back and forth since this would be on a mobile display, and automatically select create new ticket'). So: ONE sunken pill TRACK holding two KioskChip row halves — the selected half's accent wash is the thumb, the idle half stays transparent because the track is the only sunken plane. CREATE is the position an untouched control shows, which is honest only because `null` also posts as create (kioskTicketWork) and counts as settled (isKioskTicketChoiceSettled); the HALF-FINISHED state — slid to Link with nothing picked — is what still refuses the commit. Do not mount the DESK link surface: TicketPicker / TicketPickRow / DenseComposeSearchInput / SearchableSelectField (ClaimModeSelect) are desk-micro chrome built for a mouse, and a candidate list on a counter tablet is CARDS (SURFACE_LAW §5), the KioskCartLineCard anatomy — hairline + MOBILE_SCAN_ROW_CORNER, title line, facts as KioskChip meta chips. Do not re-implement the search: the debounce / abort / error-mapping / stale-result rules are the shared useTicketSearch, adapted by useKioskTicketSearch (URL + kioskFetchHealed transport are the ONLY kiosk-specific parts) — the same split useClaimTicketSearch made for a carton. The decision is a VISIT fact on the session root (`ticketChoice`), never a cart-line payload field: `ticketWork` is transaction-level and fans out to one outbox row per repair. A picked ticket outlives a re-search (the hook's own `selectedTicket` is unused here) and outranks the ticket-number PROJECTION on the paperwork, because ATTACH_TICKET stamps repair_service.ticket_number with it.
KioskTicketStep.law: src/components/kiosk/KioskTicketStep.tsx · src/components/kiosk/useKioskTicketSearch.ts · src/lib/kiosk/repair-ticket-choice.ts · GET /api/kiosk/repair/ticket-candidates · kiosk-ticket-step.test.ts (7 contracts) + repair-ticket-choice.test.ts (7 behaviours). Operator 2026-09-15. Mounted under the SignaturePad on KioskRepairPane's Review & sign (step 4 of 4); a settled answer is half of repairStepGates[3], the other half being the signature. That step's floor commits with ONE orange key — Button variant="warning" + KIOSK_POS_CTA, 'Submit repair' — and its heading row carries the labelled Print CTA on the right.

KioskCustomerIntake.useWhen: kiosk customer intake, capture customer name phone email address, counter tablet customer block
KioskCustomerIntake.doNot: ONE intake face across every kiosk channel (repair · buyback · pickup · cart) — do not write a second name/phone/email block. `fields` picks which of the four are asked; `entry` switches the control to the KIOSK_POS_ENTRY face. The form control is KioskEntryField (`src/components/kiosk/KioskEntryField.tsx`), never a raw <input> and never the desk field primitives: KIOSK_POS_ENTRY holds the 16px floor that stops iOS from zooming the whole surface on focus (COUNTER_MIN_FIELD_TEXT_PX). Phone is the MATCH KEY — it is the only blocking customer field (visit-triage `target: 'customer'`); name, email and address are warnings and must not gate a step or a submit.
KioskCustomerIntake.law: src/components/kiosk/KioskCustomerIntake.tsx + KioskCustomerIntake.test.ts · src/lib/kiosk/visit-triage.ts. Operator: 'intake their information like name, email address, phone number, address'.

KioskEntryField.useWhen: kiosk entry field, kiosk form field, kiosk text input, placeholder-in-box input on a tablet, kiosk notes textarea, signer name on a kiosk-face sign-off, desk pickup signer / decline reason field
KioskEntryField.doNot: Never a raw <input>/<textarea> and never the desk field primitives on a kiosk-face flow: every input answers to KIOSK_POS_ENTRY / KIOSK_POS_ENTRY_AREA (16px floor — no iOS focus zoom). No floating label; the placeholder is the prompt and the sr-only <label> is the accessible name. Pass `idScope` whenever the same `name` repeats on one screen. Import it from its own module, not through KioskCustomerIntake — that module binds the kiosk session store, and a desk flow must not pull the counter's cart root to get a text field.

StaffChoiceRowButton.doNot: The row IS the card — rounded-xl border, its own surface; never wrap it in a second card and never inset it in a parent outline. Never disable a row and never gate the tap behind a chip: the 'Tap to set up' PIN chip was removed 2026-09-15 (pinless act-as era; operator: 'remove the tap to set up pin. It is not needed at this dog food stage'). `pill` carries PASSIVE state only. aria-label is always 'Sign in as {name}, {role}'. One tap = one commit.

StaffPickerList.useWhen: staff roster list, switch staff list, sign-in staff picker, person list with search, recent and all staff groups
StaffPickerList.doNot: Inside a sheet/dialog pass `flat` — the rows are self-carded (see StaffChoiceRowButton), so a parent Panel/outline around them is a DUPLICATE outline (operator 2026-09-15: 'remove the parent outline. SwitchStaffSheet.doNot: PINLESS — no StaffPinPad mount, no PIN step: tap = POST /api/auth/act-as-staff { staffId, deviceKind: 'station' } with persistent inherited server-side — the same mint the email login's staff picker uses. EvidenceDisclosure.useWhen: evidence column, Selected-order column, fact row, fact that expands, collapsible evidence section, Labels / Price / Customer block, label value plus minus, disclosure row, to-ship evidence, trailing glyph, right edge alignment
EvidenceDisclosure.doNot: Do not hand-roll a <details> fact or section beside these — EvidenceFactRow (label · value), EvidenceFactDisclosure (label · value · +/−, expands in place) and EvidenceDisclosure (label · summary · +/−) own the w-24 label lane and the trailing cell. Every right-edge glyph of a record row or evidence fact (+/−, open ↗, edit ✎, the price Items chevron) sits in RECORD_TRAILING_CELL_CLASS — one 32px cell flush with the content edge, 14px glyph centred — so they stack on one vertical axis. A glyph drawn INSIDE another control (SearchableSelectField ⌄) lands on that axis with RECORD_TRAILING_GLYPH_INSET_CLASS, never its own pr-*/mr-*/ml-auto. Never repeat the summary/value inside the expanded body. The triage stack (RecordEvidence's EvidenceSection / EvidenceFact) is the non-disclosing sibling — do not mix the two in one column.
EvidenceDisclosure.law: src/design-system/components/record-ledger/EvidenceDisclosure.tsx + src/design-system/tokens/industrial-record.ts (RECORD_TRAILING_CELL_CLASS, RECORD_TRAILING_GLYPH_INSET_CLASS).
